notes: 1) SCOPE: flat targets CSV only — no FTM ownership/relationship graph; corporate-network and family/associate edges require the separate entities.ftm.json load. 2) IDENTIFIERS column is a semicolon-delimited blob mixing tax IDs, registration numbers, passport numbers, and other codes with no type labels on 727k of 1.28M rows; it cannot be used as a typed join key without regex/format sniffing per value. 3) PROGRAM_IDS present on only ~165k rows (~13%), so most non-sanctioned PEP rows carry no program code. 4) This registration reflects a single point-in-time pull despite OpenSanctions publishing daily updates; investigators should note staleness risk and re-pull before time-sensitive work. 5) Overlap with 'intl_opensanctions' (sanctions-only, ~80k targets) is expected; deduplication logic needed before combining. 6) DATASET column (semicolon-delimited per row) is the primary provenance filter to distinguish, e.g., UN sanctions rows from PEP-only rows. 7) 'epstein_relevant' rated maybe because PEP and criminal-context listings could surface associates, but no direct Epstein-network data is known to be present. ROW-COUNT RECONCILIATION (why 1,281,846 landed rows looks short of the source CSV physical line count): the downloaded CSV (opensanctions_targets.csv) has 1,304,133 physical lines (header + 1,304,132 data lines by wc -l), but pandas.read_csv (RFC4180-aware quoting) parses exactly 1,281,846 logical rows -- a 22,286-line gap. Root cause confirmed by direct inspection: embedded newline characters WITHIN quoted CSV field values -- 6,180 rows have an embedded newline in SANCTIONS, 3 in IDENTIFIERS, 3 in PHONES (multi-line sanction-program text) -- so wc -l (which counts physical newlines) over-counts these multi-line quoted records relative to true CSV row count. This is NOT a load-time drop or dedup: ingest.py._load_landing performs a plain write_pandas(auto_create_table=True, overwrite=True) with no dedup logic of its own. Verified zero rows lost across every stage: pandas-parsed row count (1,281,846) == Snowflake landed COUNT(*) (1,281,846) == COUNT(DISTINCT ID) (1,281,846, zero duplicate ids).

volume: ~300–500M+ event rows historically; ~96 new file triplets (export/mentions/gkg) added per day; individual GKG files can exceed 10 MB compressed
notes: GDELT extracts events algorithmically from open-web news using NLP/CAMEO coding; entity resolution is noisy and actors may be misidentified or conflated. Country-code joins are reliable only at the national level—sub-national geography requires the GKG or additional disambiguation. Coverage is heavily weighted toward English-language and Western media, with gaps in non-indexed outlets. Duplicate event records are common across the 15-minute files; deduplication on GLOBALEVENTID is essential before aggregation. GKG data can be extremely large (multi-GB per day) and requires significant compute to process at scale. This source reflects media coverage, not ground truth—absence of events in GDELT does not mean events did not occur.

volume: millions of case records (EOIR has processed 5+ million cases historically)
notes: Data is FOIA-derived and may carry redactions, inconsistent case ID formats across release cohorts, or lag beyond the stated monthly cadence depending on EOIR processing. Country-of-origin fields may use inconsistent ISO coding or legacy country names (e.g., pre-split nations). Case-level linkage across time periods requires careful deduplication; a single alien may have multiple case records. Disposition categories and hearing-type codes have changed over EOIR's history, requiring a data dictionary pinned to release version. Coverage begins around FY1983 but reliability improves post-2000.

volume: dozens of summary statistics tables; not row-level inmate records
notes: Data is aggregate only — no individual inmate records are exposed, limiting person-level investigation without pairing with court or PACER records. Monthly updates may not reflect mid-month transfers or population spikes. FIPS codes apply to facility locations, so joining on FIPS conflates county geography with facility jurisdiction — verify mapping logic carefully. Epstein relevance is indirect: BOP would have held jurisdiction over him at MCC New York (a federal facility), so aggregate staffing and population data for that facility could contextualize conditions at the time of his death, but individual-level data is not available here.

volume: hundreds to low thousands of aggregated rows per dashboard panel; not row-level microdata

AOR boundaries do not align with state or county lines, complicating geographic joins to other datasets.

volume: ~500,000–2,000,000 rows per fiscal year across all programs combined; each program file ranges from tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of rows

Dataset quality and completeness vary significantly by publisher — federal datasets tend to be more structured and machine-readable than municipal ones. EXEMPTION_REINSTATEMENT_DATE often blank (org never reinstated). chunked:true required for 1.2M rows; low_memory(default) is ignored under chunksize - no conflict (tested). volume: ~50-100 data tables per yearbook edition; each table ranges from dozens to thousands of rows; ~29 yearbook editions available

GFI estimates are derived from mirror-trade statistics (comparing partner-reported import/export values) and carry well-documented methodological limitations: they capture discrepancies that may include legitimate measurement error, not solely illicit flows. Coverage is uneven across countries and years; updates are irregular and often lag several years behind the reference period. Figures should be treated as order-of-magnitude indicators rather than precise illicit-flow measurements. GFI revised its methodology in 2017, so pre- and post-2017 estimates are not directly comparable.

volume: 1,727+ report files in the data library; individual files range from ~20 KB to ~766 KB; row counts per file typically in the hundreds to low thousands

volume: ~500,000+ documents historically; ~50-200 new documents per Federal Register publication day; paginated at 100 per page

Document metadata (agency names, docket IDs) may be inconsistently formatted across time periods, complicating joins. volume: Millions of rows across all hospital MRFs; individual hospital files range from thousands to hundreds of thousands of rows
notes: Hospital compliance with the CMS price transparency rule has been inconsistent; many MRFs are malformed, incomplete, or hosted at unstable URLs, requiring significant normalization effort before analysis. Negotiated rates may be expressed as percentages, multipliers, or flat amounts, complicating cross-hospital comparisons. NPIs link to facility or billing-group level, not always to the ultimate corporate owner, so a corporate-ownership join (e.g., to CMS PECOS or state filings) is needed to attribute rates to parent entities.
